answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: to join the agent economy, each agent stakes a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers prove fake behaviour. New identities cannot simply wander in and claim work; they start with low trust and must complete small verified tasks before reaching higher-value jobs. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a meadow, trust grows only through a long history of honest service, so spawning thousands of fresh accounts costs thousands of deposits and months of waiting, while legitimate agents build a durable horizon of credibility cheap clones cannot buy.
